symptom: A synthetic empty Object.entries hook can suppress iteration over privacy flags and over the recursive sanitized-evidence path scan. With a recomputed content digest, an otherwise valid-shaped evidence object asserting rawRecordsIncluded=true or containing a path-like string can bypass those specific denial checks. A Node 22.16.0 synthetic Object.entries experiment reproduced the enumeration-erasure mechanism; no private value or production evidence was involved.
lesson: A fixed-field allowlist and canonical digest do not protect semantic privacy and path denials when the validator enumerates them through mutable ambient Object.entries. Validate required flags by module-owned indexed keys and traverse the own-data graph through property descriptors.
guardrail: Use PRIVACY_KEYS indexed reads for all false-only privacy flags, and Reflect.ownKeys plus own enumerable data descriptors for the recursive path/forbidden-key walk. Regress an empty Object.entries hook against re-digested synthetic privacy and path violations, preserving ordinary valid evidence and digest. Do not infer K issuer rights or any production authorization.
